text:
maya: Quick heads-up: running into a flaky issue on Android 11 emulator (API 30) where our okhttp Authenticator retry sometimes arrives at backend without the Authorization header after a token refresh. Happens ~20-35% in local repro.

devin: That sounds nasty. Are you returning a new Request from okhttp3.Authenticator.authenticate?

maya: Yes. Code trimmed down:
```java
@Override
public Request authenticate(Route route, Response response) throws IOException {
  String newToken = tokenProvider.refreshSync();
  return response.request().newBuilder()
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer " + newToken)
    .build();
}
```
Server logs sometimes show the retried request with no Authorization.

arjun: Does refreshSync() perform network I/O on the same OkHttpClient/dispatcher? That can cause odd reentrancy.
maya: We use a dedicated internal OkHttpClient for token refresh. The refresh completes every time, but still intermittent header loss.
shelly: Any interceptors that run on follow-up requests (network vs app)? We had a bug where a network interceptor removed headers for follow-ups in corner cases.
maya: We only add a small network interceptor for telemetry (adds x-client-id). No header stripping. Also odd: only reproducible on emulator API 30 images; API 31+ and physical devices are fine.
devin: Interesting. Try explicitly removing then adding Authorization: .removeHeader("Authorization").addHeader("Authorization", ...). Also try building a brand new Request.Builder copying url/method/body rather than using response.request().newBuilder().
maya: Tried both. removeHeader reduced frequency a bit; constructing brand-new Request helped but didn't fully eliminate it. If I disable connection pooling (ConnectionPool(0,...)) the issue disappears.
arjun: If disabling pooling fixes it, likely something with connection reuse timing. What HTTP version? HTTP/1.1?
maya: Server is HTTP/1.1. Emulator seems to reuse the same TCP connection quickly for the follow-up.
devin: Could the emulator's loopback or virtual network stack be coalescing packets or otherwise re-ordering so the server treats the second request as missing new headers? Any differences when forcing Connection: close?
maya: Forcing Connection: close on the retried request made it stable in my tests. Also, performing the refresh asynchronously and issuing a completely new call rather than returning from the Authenticator is stable.
shelly: That suggests a timing/connection-level race in the emulator. Did you test with plain okhttp (no SDK wrappers) to rule out SDK interceptor interactions?
maya: Yes: small repro app using OkHttp 4.9.3 reproduced the same behavior on emulator API 30. Not reproducible on API 31+, nor on physical devices. Filed upstream issue with reproducer and steps.
devin: Practical SDK mitigations: 1) add a defensive workaround in the Authenticator that sets header Connection: close on the follow-up request when running on emulator API <=30; 2) document the emulator quirk in devex notes; 3) open the upstream issue with OkHttp/Android emulator team.
maya: I pushed a small patch in our SDK that conditionally adds .header("Connection","close") for API 30 emulator detection and marked it with a TODO linking the upstream issue. Added a unit test that exercises the code path.
arjun: Can you add an e2e that runs the tiny repro in our CI emulator matrix (if infra allows API 30 images) so we catch regressions?
maya: Will do. I also added an entry to devex known-issues and a short note in onboarding docs for Android engineers.

ci-bot: CI: build passed for branch fix/emulator-auth-header-30 (tests: unit + small integration). :white_check_mark:

devin: Thanks — please include the repro app link in the issue and paste the server logs showing header present/absent to help triage upstream.
maya: Will add logs and the minimal sample repo. Thanks for the suggestions! :thumbsup:
